clue.text: The final battle needs a weapon–old, like Quixote.

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
aged means old
Don Quixote bears the Spanish title don, so a don is someone like him

explanation.surface: A grim prophecy: the last war on earth calls for an antique weapon, as wielded by Cervantes's deluded knight.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation, Armageddon is the site of the climactic conflict at the end of the world.

clue.text: They think about the origins of man, being people who make excuses about the North, in a way.

definitions.text: They think about the origins of man

indicators.note: the excuse-makers go about, that is around, the northern route, which sits after their first letter

parts.note: apologists are people who defend or excuse something
N is the abbreviation for north
thro is a poetic short form of through, meaning by way of

explanation.surface: Scholars of human origins described as excuse-makers on a northern route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' means the excuse-makers wrap around the northern route; 'in a way' is THRO, the old poetic short form of through.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropologists study humankind, including its evolutionary beginnings.

clue.text: Intended to show up the first person objectively with a worker type to finish it.

parts.note: me is the object form of the first-person pronoun
a worker ant is a type of ant
taken as written

explanation.surface: Meant to expose oneself, paired with a labourer who will wrap up the job.
explanation.definitionFit: If you meant to do something, it was your purpose or plan.

clue.text: A thousand to one that it's disappeared!

parts.note: G, for grand, is a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A betting-odds exclamation: a thousand to one it has vanished!
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' is only a link, though it mimics the language of odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone has vanished or ceased to be present.

clue.text: Being such, has a habit such as a soldier gets right. (This up is spit and polish; down is punishment.)

definitions.text: Being such, has a habit such as a soldier gets right. (This up is spit and polish; down is punishment.)

parts.words: Being such, has a habit such as a soldier gets right. (This up is spit and polish; down is punishment.)
parts.note: a word for clothed, as in wearing a habit; soldiers dress ranks with 'right dress'; with up it means smartened, with down it means scolded

explanation.walkthrough: A habit is a garment, and 'right dress' is the drill order that aligns soldiers; the bracket gives the two phrasal verbs, dressed up and dressed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed means wearing clothes; dressed up is smartly turned out, and a dressing-down is a severe reprimand.

clue.text: Turns something to show a different surface.

definitions.text: Turns something to show a different surface.

parts.words: Turns something to show a different surface.
parts.note: the dictionary sense of a rare verb, related to obverse, the face of a coin

explanation.walkthrough: This is a plain definition of an uncommon word: to obvert is to turn something so another face shows.
explanation.definitionFit: Obvert is a formal verb for turning an object round so that a different side faces outward.

clue.text: Badly need a garden spot?

indicators.note: the word need is treated badly, its letters knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A question about whether some poorly kept patch of garden is really needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical paradise garden, so it is the garden spot above all others.

clue.text: Dear me! It's wrong, yet gets right asleep if you are one–

indicators.note: the letters of dear me are wrongly placed and need sorting

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is amiss, then it comes right in sleep, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone who dreams, which happens while asleep.

clue.text: and little Clara was a 7 in this.

definitions.text: and little Clara was a 7 in this.

parts.words: and little Clara was a 7 in this.
parts.note: carries on from 7-down; Clara is the girl whose dream makes up the Tchaikovsky ballet

explanation.walkthrough: In The Nutcracker, young Clara dreams the whole fantasy, so she is a dreamer in Tchaikovsky's music; the suite is the concert version of the ballet's music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nutcracker Suite is Tchaikovsky's suite from the ballet in which Clara dreams.

clue.text: Suggesting a meaning, and being in such a little state got in wrong to make it.

parts.note: Conn. abbreviates Connecticut, a small US state

indicators.note: the letters of got in are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Implying something, while in a small state that went in badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To connote is to imply an associated meaning beyond the literal one.

clue.text: One who is new on the job, with the following having a couple of failing marks.

definitions.text: One who is new on the job

parts.note: a train is a retinue, the people following someone
E is a failing grade in a school, so two of them are EE

explanation.surface: A new hire whose first report card shows a pair of poor grades.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is a newcomer still being taught the work, a beginner in the post.

clue.text: Something pretty in the garden has a point near the end, which is rather uncontrolled in character.

indicators.note: the point goes in close to the end of the flower's name, before its last letter

parts.note: a violet is a pretty garden flower
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A garden flower with a thorny tip turns out to have a wild nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone violent acts with unrestrained force, lacking self-control in temperament.

clue.text: A starburst, darn it…

indicators.note: the word star bursts apart and its letters land in a new order

parts.note: the first half of the word starburst; that the answer also reads backwards inside starburst is a coincidence of the anagram

explanation.surface: An exclamation of annoyance at a firework's starburst going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starburst' reads as one word, but split it: 'star' is the fodder and 'burst' the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats! is a mild oath of frustration, the same exclamation as darn it.

clue.text: … for one who might be used to starbursts!

definitions.text: … for one who might be used to starbursts!

parts.words: … for one who might be used to starbursts!
parts.note: following on from the previous clue, the person who studies exploding stars

explanation.walkthrough: It continues 12-across: starbursts here are bursts of star formation in galaxies, the kind of thing a stargazing scientist is used to.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientist who studies celestial objects, starbursts among them.

clue.text: See 24
Supported by a bit of stage ware, having a classical foot here.

parts.note: a prop is an item used on stage in a play
ped- is the stem of Latin pes, foot, as in pedal

explanation.surface: A theatre set where everything rests on a piece of scenery with an ancient pillar foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop something is to hold it up, so propped means held up or supported.

clue.text: With a certain amount of irony.

definitions.text: With a certain amount of irony.

parts.words: With a certain amount of irony.
parts.note: describes writing that mocks with a measure of irony, as satire does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Irony' could suggest iron content, as in a metal; the sense meant is mocking wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire works through ridicule and irony, so a satiric piece carries a good share of it.

clue.text: Inside–sometimes outside — material.

parts.note: fabric sewn inside garments, which on reversible clothes ends up on the outside

explanation.walkthrough: A reversible coat can be worn inside out, which puts the inner fabric on show.
explanation.definitionFit: Linings are the inner layers of fabric in clothing, curtains and bags.

clue.text: Possibly vain, and a nice season in Paris shows a certain amount of simplicity.

indicators.note: the letters of vain are possibly arranged another way

parts.note: été is French for summer, a pleasant season

explanation.surface: A conceited person enjoying a lovely French summer turns out to be rather unsophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is an artless, unworldly innocence, a lack of sophistication.

clue.text: How some meetings break up with a bad act having a point to pass on.

parts.note: a sin is a wrongful act
E, east, is a compass point
to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A meeting ends acrimoniously after someone behaves badly and wants to move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine die is Latin for without a day: a body adjourning so has set no date to reconvene.

clue.text: Any vertebrate of the reptile, bird and mammal class, but the main sort has a broken toe.

definitions.text: Any vertebrate of the reptile, bird and mammal class

indicators.note: to sort the letters of main is to rearrange them
the letters of toe are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A zoology lesson in which the chief example has an injured toe.
explanation.definitionFit: Amniotes are the vertebrates whose embryos develop in an amnion: reptiles, birds and mammals.

clue.text: Behave in a way, when about to steal a type that belongs in the circus.

definitions.text: type that belongs in the circus

indicators.note: act goes about, or around, the theft word and the following a

parts.note: to act is to behave in a particular way
to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Someone behaving shiftily as they prepare to steal turns out to be a big-top performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' signals that the behaving word goes around the stealing word and the a; 'when' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs tumbling and balancing feats, a classic circus artist.

clue.text: A bad poet is all mixed up about age. What a way to run things!

indicators.note: the scrambled poet goes about, or around, the age
a bad poet garbles the word itself, so its letters are muddled
a second signal that the letters of poet are scrambled

parts.note: an era is an age

explanation.surface: A poor versifier is confused about the times, and that is no way to manage affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Two signals, 'bad' and 'is all mixed up', scramble the poet into OPTE; 'about' then wraps OPTE around the age word. 'What a way to' is surface padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a business or machine is to manage it and keep it running.

clue.text: Starts good with those who are hearing things that are the shining type.

definitions.text: things that are the shining type

indicators.note: the start of the word good gives its first letter

parts.note: first letter of good
listeners are people who hear

explanation.surface: A good start among people who imagine voices, then a turn to shiny objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' takes the first letter of good; 'hearing things' suggests hallucinating, but 'things' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Glisteners are things that glisten, that is sparkle or shine.

clue.text: Things laid down at the track, possibly.

definitions.text: Things laid down at the track, possibly.

parts.words: Things laid down at the track, possibly.
parts.note: railway sleepers or rails are laid at a track, but so are wagers at a racetrack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid down' and 'track' suggest building a railway; one lays a bet, and the track is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Bets are wagers placed, or laid, on the outcome of a race.

clue.text: How many stories start, formerly not down–no, up–and a mite different.

parts.note: once means formerly, at some earlier time
the opposite of down is up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word no is read upward, backwards
the letters of mite are made different by rearranging

explanation.surface: A storyteller's opening, tangled in directions and a small creature changing.
explanation.definitionFit: Once upon a time is the traditional opening phrase of fairy tales.

clue.text: Got mad about what they did to the clams?

definitions.text: what they did to the clams?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: clams are cooked by steaming

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal kitchen sense of the word, alongside its slang sense of fuming.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steamed is slang for being furious, and steamed clams are a classic seafood dish.

clue.text: An Indic language, used by Franklin, such as Sal, and myself.

parts.note: Benjamin Franklin is known as Ben
Sal is a girl's name, so she is a gal
I is the speaker, myself

explanation.surface: A language spoken by Ben Franklin, a girl called Sal and the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the Indo-Aryan language of Bangladesh and West Bengal.

clue.text: A forward movement when the favorites return.

indicators.note: the favourites word comes back, read from the end

parts.note: a teacher's pets are their favourites

explanation.surface: Progress made when the most favoured people come back.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace forward, and figuratively a move of progress.

clue.text: What one peels with steady and astute watchfulness.

definitions.text: What one peels with steady and astute watchfulness.

parts.words: What one peels with steady and astute watchfulness.
parts.note: you keep your eyes peeled to watch out; this particular one is the alert eye a sailor keeps on the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Peels' points to the idiom 'keep your eyes peeled'; the eye in question is the one kept on the skies for changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a weather eye open is to stay alert and watchful for trouble, as sailors watch for storms.
